subject: Boundary Controls: SSO, SCIM & Service Account Orchestration for Edge IP Allowlist
messages:
From: Sam Jackson <sam.jackson@edgefin.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, security@edgefin.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Access gating & provisioning kickoff (EdgeFin)

Hi Kimberly / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. EdgeFin is ready to move from discovery to an implementation run: SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, IP allowlist for our edge gateways for production traffic, and a small set of service accounts for automation. High level asks:

- Minimal downtime for SSO cutover (can we support a staged ramp?)
- SCIM mapping for groups: admins / devs / readonly
- IP allowlist: we will require per-region CIDR blocks and an emergency bypass plan
- Service accounts: short-lived keys preferred; well need a template policy

Id like to schedule a 45-min technical kickoff with your implementation lead + our infra/security. Could you propose slots in the next 48 hours? Im ccing our security mailbox with the initial list of questions. Attaching a top-level matrix (sent as separate file).

Sam
Security & Infrastructure, EdgeFin
(attachment: edgefin-sso-scim-matrix.xlsx)

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 11:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: EdgeFin pre-kickoff checklist

Kim / Ben / Marissa,

I did a quick review of Sams matrix. A few engineering notes so were aligned for the kickoff:

- SAML: EdgeFin uses Okta as IdP and requires NameID as transient for SSO (not persistent). We need to confirm SAML binding preference (POST vs Redirect) and signature algorithm (sha256).
- SCIM: they have nested groups; Redwood SCIM currently supports group->member mapping but not arbitrary nested groups. We can support a one-level flattening (group.name -> group.members). Need to confirm if EdgeFin can accept that mapping.
- IP allowlist: they mentioned per-region CIDRs. Ben, Ill need the exact egress/ingress ports we lock down for inference endpoints. Ill map that to our load-balancer IP targets.
- Service accounts: We prefer ephemeral keys with a short TTL (12 hours) for automation tokens. For long-running jobs we can create named service accounts with scoped permissions. We should provide an example IAM policy.

Action items for kickoff:
1) Get Okta metadata file + contact for SAML certificate rotation (Sam to provide).
2) Agree SCIM attribute set: displayName, email, externalId, groups (flattening rule).
3) EdgeFin to provide allowed CIDRs and emergency bypass SOP.
4) Prepare service-account templates + rotation script (Ben).

Ill draft the engineering section of the runbook pre-meeting.

-jb
Jordan Blake
Senior Implementation Engineer, Redwood
(attachment: none)

- SCIM nesting: we can export a flattened groups view if thats the recommended approach; Ill ask our IdP team to prepare that extract.
- IP allowlist: we have 3 region blocks (us-west2, us-east1, eu-west1). Ill send the exact CIDRs in a separate email (attaching here). Also please confirm: do you support dynamic egress from Redwood that would require updating our firewall?

Attaching a text file with the CIDRs and a preliminary contact list.

Anne / team,

Thanks for the CIDRs. Quick answers:
- Redwoods hosted inference egress is from a documented set of ASNs and IP ranges; we can provide a refreshable list and a webhook to notify you before a change. That means your firewall needs a small set of allow entries we maintain centrally.
- For the cutover plan we recommend staged traffic split by percentage across SSO sessions to catch edge cases (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with health checks at each step. This avoids a full downtime cutover.
- Service accounts: attaching a one-page policy template and a short rotation script that uses our token-issuing API. Were set to demo the script in the kickoff.

Attachments: service-account-policy-v1.pdf (policy), rotation-sample.sh (inline during demo).

Ill bring the runbook section with the firewall webhook link and the stepwise cutover checklist.

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood
